ucat_requirements.role_detail: UCAT is used as a pass/fail section threshold (minimum 500 in each of the three cognitive sections) plus an annually-recalculated overall cut-off score used to rank and select applicants for interview. There is NO published combined academic-score + UCAT weighted formula for A100.
ucat_requirements.section_threshold: Minimum 500 in each individual cognitive section (Verbal Reasoning, Decision Making, Quantitative Reasoning).
ucat_requirements.overall_threshold: Recalculated every year based on the strength of that year's applicant pool; not fixed in advance and not predictable from prior years (university's own caveat).
ucat_requirements.ranking_mechanism: Each applicant who meets the academic entry criteria is ranked by UCAT score; interview places are allocated to the highest UCAT scorers within each category (Home/Overseas x Non-graduate/Graduate) until interview capacity is filled, because of separate overseas (~9%) and graduate (~25%) number-control caps.
ucat_requirements.combined_formula_statement: The university does not publish a mathematical interview-selection formula combining academic score and UCAT score. Selection to interview for A100 is: (1) meet academic threshold (pass/fail, e.g. predicted/achieved AAA + GCSE profile) -> (2) rank purely by UCAT total score within applicant category -> (3) invite to interview until places fill.
ucat_requirements.sjt_role: For 2026 entry, City St George's states it will consider SJT Banding scores in decision-making, but does not publish an exact band cut-off or the precise mechanism (pass/fail band vs. scored input) in the sources reviewed.

ucat_historical_thresholds.scale_note: Per university publication and UCAT Consortium test-format history: cycles 2016-2025 are on the pre-2025 four-subtest scale (1200-3600, later effectively out of ~3600 after a section change in 2017); cycle 2026 is the first year on the new three-subtest scale (900-2700, Abstract Reasoning removed). The University's own table already reflects this scale change (2026 values are far lower in absolute terms, consistent with the smaller 2700 maximum).

converted_to_current_2700_scale.reason: No official UCAT Consortium-published conversion table or methodology for converting pre-2025 (four-subtest, ~1200-3600) scores to the post-2025 (three-subtest, 900-2700) scale was located. UCAT Consortium's own published materials (ucat.ac.uk) describe the new 900-2700 scoring structure but do not publish an official historical conversion table; third-party tutoring companies publish unofficial 'percentile-matching' or 'same-cohort re-scoring' conversions, but these are explicitly not endorsed by the UCAT Consortium and vary between providers (e.g. some warn that a flat multiplier such as x0.75 is inaccurate by 20-25 points). Per the sourcing rules governing this report, no conversion ratio has been invented or applied. The 2016-2025 figures above are presented on their originally-published (old) scale only, alongside the 2026 figure which is already on the new scale, exactly as the university published them.

sjt_policy.note: University states only that SJT Banding will be 'considered in our decision making' for 2026 entry; no further mechanism, band threshold, or scoring detail is published.

interview_prediction_bands.university: City St George's, University of London
interview_prediction_bands.status: APPLYSMART-DERIVED ESTIMATE — NOT AN OFFICIAL UNIVERSITY OR UCAT CONSORTIUM PRODUCT
interview_prediction_bands.university_warning_verbatim: It is not possible to predict what the UCAT thresholds will be in any individual year, nor to use data from previous years to predict subsequent years' thresholds. The number and quality of applications can vary year-on-year and the selection process is reviewed annually and may be subject to change.

methodology.description: Interview-prediction bands are NOT published by the university. This config builds a heuristic banding tool by measuring an applicant's raw UCAT total against the single most recent officially published cut-off for their category (2026 entry, the only cycle so far on the current 900-2700 scale), with band widths set from the observed year-on-year VOLATILITY of the university's own historical cut-offs (see volatility_context). Because SGUL explicitly states prior-year cut-offs cannot predict future ones, every band below is a probability-style heuristic, not a guarantee, and should be surfaced to users with the university_warning_verbatim text attached at all times.
gate_conditions_before_banding_applies: Academic threshold must be met (pass/fail per Section 4 of the main report) — banding is meaningless if this gate fails, since academically-ineligible applicants are not ranked at all.
All three UCAT section scores must be >= 500 — this is a hard per-section gate independent of the overall-score banding below.
Applicant must be correctly assigned to one of the four ranking categories (Home Non-Grad / Home Grad / Overseas Non-Grad / Overseas Grad), since each is ranked and cut off separately.
methodology.scale_note: Bands below are expressed on the CURRENT UCAT scale (900-2700, three cognitive subtests: Verbal Reasoning, Decision Making, Quantitative Reasoning), which has applied since the test sat in 2025 (i.e. for 2026 entry onward). Do NOT compare a score on this scale against any pre-2026 published SGUL cut-off (2016-2025 figures were on the old ~3600 scale) — see the main report's Section 10 on why no official conversion exists between the two scales.

volatility_context.description: Year-on-year change in SGUL's own published overall UCAT cut-offs, old scale (2020-2025, Home Non-Graduate main-cycle figure), used only to size band widths — NOT itself a prediction.
volatility_context.interpretation: On the old ~3600-point scale, SGUL's Home Non-Graduate cut-off moved by 60-140 points (roughly 1.7%-3.9% of the scale) from one cycle to the next. This report scales that same PERCENTAGE volatility onto the current 2700-point scale (since no official points-based conversion exists) to size the bands below, rather than reusing the old raw point-swings directly.

scaled_swing_estimate_2700_basis.calculation_note: average_absolute_swing_points (92) / 3600 * 2700 ≈ 69; max_observed_swing_points (140) / 3600 * 2700 ≈ 105. This is an ApplySmart-derived scaling for band-width purposes only, explicitly NOT an official UCAT Consortium or university conversion of actual score meaning (see main report Section 10).

band_definitions.label: Very likely to clear the UCAT cut-off
band_definitions.description: At least ~105 points (the largest observed year-on-year swing, rescaled to the 2700 basis) above the most recent published category cut-off. Historically, a margin this size has exceeded every observed year-on-year cut-off movement.
band_definitions.not_a_guarantee_note: Interview places are still filled by ranking, not by clearing an absolute score — a very strong applicant pool in a given cycle could still push the actual cut-off above this band. Always pair with the university_warning_verbatim text.

band_definitions.label: Likely to clear the UCAT cut-off
band_definitions.description: Above the reference cut-off by more than the average observed swing (~69, rounded to 30 as a conservative lower band edge) but less than the maximum observed swing.

band_definitions.label: Borderline — within typical year-on-year cut-off movement
band_definitions.description: Within one average historical swing (±69 points) of the reference cut-off in either direction. Whether this applicant would have been invited is genuinely uncertain and highly dependent on that cycle's applicant pool strength.

band_definitions.label: Below typical year-on-year cut-off movement
band_definitions.description: Below the reference cut-off by more than one average swing but within the maximum observed swing. Would need a materially weaker applicant pool than any seen in the historical data to clear.

band_definitions.label: Well below typical year-on-year cut-off movement
band_definitions.description: More than the largest observed historical swing below the reference cut-off.
band_definitions.predicted_likelihood_label: Very unlikely under the current process

reference_cutoffs_2026_entry_current_sca.note: These are the ONLY published cut-offs on the current 900-2700 scale (2026 entry, the first cycle on this scale). Because there is only one data point per category on this scale, band widths are necessarily borrowed from old-scale volatility (see volatility_context) rather than calculated from multiple current-scale years. Confidence in these bands should be treated as LOW until at least 2-3 more cycles of current-scale data are published.

sjt_interaction.note: For 2026 entry, SGUL states SJT Banding (the UCAT Consortium's own Band 1-4 scale, separate from the 900-2700 cognitive total) is 'considered in decision making,' but the mechanism is not published. This interview_prediction_bands config therefore does NOT adjust its A-E bands for SJT performance. If SJT is later confirmed to gate or shift the cut-off, this config will need a documented multiplier or override rule at that time — do not invent one now.
sjt_interaction.sjt_scale_reference: UCAT Consortium SJT bands run 1 (highest) to 4 (lowest), reported separately from the 900-2700 cognitive total.

applysmart_usage_notes: Always display the university_warning_verbatim text alongside any band output shown to a user — this is a heuristic, not a university-endorsed prediction.

Do not let this config be used to compare a pre-2026 UCAT score (old ~3600 scale) directly against these bands — route old-scale scores through a clearly-labelled 'legacy scale, not comparable' message instead of silently converting.

Re-run computed_band_ranges_by_category once the 2027-entry cut-off is published, and recompute volatility_context on TWO current-scale data points at that stage rather than continuing to borrow the old-scale swing estimate.

This config predicts INTERVIEW INVITATION likelihood only (Stage 1 ranking). It says nothing about eventual OFFER likelihood, since no published post-interview scoring formula exists (see main report Section 15).
interview_prediction_bands.confidence_level: LOW — based on a single current-scale data point per category and a cross-scale volatility estimate; treat as an illustrative heuristic pending further published cycles.

interview_prediction_engine_spec.university: City St George's, University of London
interview_prediction_engine_spec.purpose: Defines SJT handling, official contextual-group handling, four-pool routing, and mandatory academic and UCAT-section gates before band computation.

1_sjt_handling.rationale: The university confirms SJT Banding 'will be considered in decision making' for 2026 entry, but publishes no band cut-off, no pass/fail rule, and no statement of whether it gates, re-ranks, or tie-breaks. Silently omitting it (as the original banding config did) is indistinguishable from a bug. Silently modelling it would require an invented weighting. The only defensible engine behaviour is to CAPTURE the value, EXCLUDE it from the score/band computation, and SURFACE that exclusion to the caller every time.

engine_contract.reason_required_even_if_unused: So the exclusion can be logged and surfaced per-applicant, and so the field is already wired in when/if SGUL publishes a real mechanism.
engine_contract.processing_rule: sjt_band is stored on the prediction result object verbatim. It MUST NOT be added to, subtracted from, or used to filter/gate ucat_total_score, reference_cutoff, or any band boundary in this version.
engine_contract.output_flag_required: sjt_excluded_from_prediction: true (hard-coded, always present on every prediction result for this university/course)
engine_contract.output_message_required: "SGUL states SJT Banding is considered in 2026-entry decisions, but has not published how. Your SJT Band 1-4 is recorded but NOT included in this prediction."

special_case_sjt_band_4.handling: No special handling applied. Do NOT auto-flag or auto-downgrade a Band 4 ("atypical") result, because no published SGUL policy on Band 4 consequences exists (confirmed absent in main report Section 8).
special_case_sjt_band_4.engine_contract_addition: If sjt_band == 4, still return the standard band_A-E result plus the standard exclusion message above — no additional warning text, no score penalty, no separate path.

future_activation.trigger_to_revisit: Official SGUL publication (course page, admissions policy PDF, or FOI response) stating the exact SJT mechanism for a given cycle.
future_activation.until_then: sjt_handling.mode must remain EXPLICITLY_EXCLUDED_PENDING_DATA. Do not switch to a modelled mode without a cited official source recorded in a new sjt_mechanism_source field.

2_contextual_applicant_routing.rationale: The official contextual policy confirms that groups 1 and 2 may receive a reduced conditional offer and pre/post-application support, while group 3 receives support only. It does not publish a lower UCAT cut-off, guaranteed interview, ranking uplift, or separate contextual interview pool. Therefore contextual status must be captured and surfaced, but must not disable or alter the standard UCAT interview prediction.

explicit_non_goals: Do not apply a lower contextual UCAT cutoff
Do not add contextual interview-ranking points
Do not disable prediction solely because the applicant is contextual

3_pool_routing_and_gate_enforcement.purpose: Guarantees the engine cannot reach band computation without first (a) correctly classifying the applicant into exactly one of the four published pools, and (b) enforcing the three per-section UCAT minimums and the academic threshold, in that order, every time.
required_input_fields: academic_threshold_met (boolean) — computed upstream from Section 4 criteria (A-level/IB/GCSE/etc.), NOT by this engine

mandatory_gate_sequence.logic: Validate contextual_status and attach the applicable contextual-offer/support metadata. Do not change UCAT band boundaries or stop prediction solely because of contextual status.

mandatory_gate_sequence.on_fail: STOP. Return prediction_status = 'NOT_APPLICABLE', reason = 'academic_threshold_not_met', user_message = "UCAT banding is only meaningful once the academic entry threshold is met — SGUL does not rank applicants who don't clear this gate." Do not compute or return any band.

mandatory_gate_sequence.gate: section_minimums: ucat_vr_score >= 500 AND ucat_dm_score >= 500 AND ucat_qr_score >= 500
mandatory_gate_sequence.on_fail: STOP. Return prediction_status = 'NOT_APPLICABLE', reason = 'ucat_section_minimum_not_met', failing_sections = [list each section below 500], user_message = "SGUL requires a minimum of 500 in every UCAT section (Verbal Reasoning, Decision Making, Quantitative Reasoning). At least one section is below this, so this applicant is not eligible for ranking regardless of overall score." Do not compute or return any band even if the overall total would otherwise land in Band A.

mandatory_gate_sequence.logic: pool = CONCAT(fee_status, '_', applicant_type), mapped to exactly one of: 'home_non_graduate' | 'home_graduate' | 'overseas_non_graduate' | 'overseas_graduate'
mandatory_gate_sequence.on_fail: STOP if fee_status or applicant_type is missing/invalid. Return prediction_status = 'NEEDS_INPUT', reason = 'pool_classification_incomplete'. Never default to a pool silently (e.g. never assume 'home_non_graduate' as a fallback default).

mandatory_gate_sequence.logic: ucat_total_score = ucat_vr_score + ucat_dm_score + ucat_qr_score. Look up computed_band_ranges_by_category[pool] from citystgeorges_a100_interview_prediction_bands.json. Assign band_id per the A-E ranges. Attach sjt_excluded_from_prediction = true and the section-1 message. Attach confidence_level = 'LOW' and the university_warning_verbatim text from the companion config, unconditionally.

self_test_requirements.description: Before this engine is considered implemented correctly, it must pass test cases confirming gate order and pool coverage — not just band-boundary arithmetic.
required_test_cases: All four pools individually produce correct band_A-E boundaries matching computed_band_ranges_by_category.
An applicant with academic_threshold_met = false receives 'NOT_APPLICABLE' / academic_threshold_not_met regardless of how high their UCAT score is.
An applicant with any single section score of 499 receives 'NOT_APPLICABLE' / ucat_section_minimum_not_met even if their overall total would be Band A.
An applicant with all three sections exactly at 500 is NOT rejected by the section-minimum gate (boundary-inclusive check).
Missing or invalid fee_status/applicant_type returns NEEDS_INPUT and never silently defaults to a pool.
sjt_band is present and echoed back on every successful prediction, with sjt_excluded_from_prediction = true and never influences band_id.
A sjt_band = 4 applicant who otherwise clears all gates receives an ordinary Band A-E result with no extra penalty or warning beyond the standard exclusion message.
contextual_status = group_1 produces the same UCAT band as an otherwise identical non-contextual applicant and attaches contextual-offer plus pre/post-support metadata.
contextual_status = group_2 produces the same UCAT band as an otherwise identical non-contextual applicant and attaches contextual-offer plus pre/post-support metadata.
contextual_status = group_3 produces the same UCAT band as an otherwise identical non-contextual applicant, sets eligible_for_contextual_offer = false, and attaches pre/post-support metadata.
contextual_status = unknown does not alter the band and surfaces contextual_eligibility_unconfirmed = true.
No contextual group changes reference_cutoff or any A-E boundary.

engine_output_schema.ucat_total_score: int|null (still returned even on NOT_APPLICABLE, for transparency)
engine_output_schema.gate_failures: array of strings, empty if none
engine_output_schema.sjt_excluded_from_prediction: boolean, always true when a band is present
engine_output_schema.confidence_level: string, always 'LOW' when a band is present
engine_output_schema.university_warning_verbatim: string, always attached when a band is present
engine_output_schema.user_message: string, human-readable explanation of the status

open_items_still_not_encoded: Exact SJT mechanism — engine explicitly excludes SJT from band computation pending a cited official rule.
No separate contextual interview-ranking mechanism is published; standard UCAT bands remain in use and no contextual cutoff adjustment is invented.
Post-interview offer prediction is out of scope because no published offer formula exists.
